title: The Penny That Wasn’t There
subtitle: 0.1 + 0.2 has opinions.
description: A shopping cart total that drifts by a fraction of a cent.
instructions: Reproduce the failure mentally or locally.
Pinpoint the exact line and mechanism of the bug.
Write the minimal fix that restores the expected behaviour.
constraints: Do not redesign the function unless the bug requires it.
hints: Which of the four numbers can be represented exactly in binary?
Delay the division: compute in the unit the input already gives you.

solution.summary: Dividing each price by 100 produces non-representable binary fractions whose errors accumulate across four additions. Keeping integer cents and dividing once confines the rounding to a single, display-level step.
approach: 0.19, 0.99, 0.49, 0.33 are all repeating values in base 2.
Each division and addition rounds to the nearest double; errors compound.
Integer arithmetic in cents is exact up to 2^53, and one final division bounds the error.

code.label: Corrected implementation

commonMistakes: Reaching for `toFixed(2)` mid-loop — it returns strings and hides the problem.
Storing money as floats at all; integers or a decimal type are the real fix.

learningObjectives: Structure money math to stay exact
